# Preparing the Two-Repository Lab

The exercises in Part II use two prepared repositories: `commercial-truck-search-api` and
`commercial-truck-search-ui`.  The backend owns the OpenAPI contract, and OpenAPI Generator
produces the TypeScript Angular client consumed by the frontend.  Before asking an agent to change
behavior, you may want to establish a baseline for both repositories.  That gives you a way to
distinguish an environment problem from a specification or implementation defect.

## Learning objective

By the end of this chapter, you should be able to clone, inspect, build, test, and run both
repositories.  You will also have a record of the tool versions, application ports, and clean
commits that can help you repeat the later exercises.

## How the lab supports the objective

- You can use the prepared repositories to keep the exercises focused on SDD rather than project
  scaffolding.
- You can keep an independent OpenSpec history beside each codebase.
- The backend can remain the API owner while the frontend client is generated from that contract.

## Backend baseline

It may help to inspect the backend before changing it.  Check the versions and tools in use: Java
21, Spring Boot 4.1.1, Maven, Spring Data JPA, and H2.  Locate the existing test conventions and
application boundaries.  Also check whether truck search has been implemented.  Later chapters
use its absence as the starting condition for the first feature.

## Frontend baseline

Inspect the frontend separately.  Check for Angular 21 and Node.js 24.19.0, then locate the
Vitest, component-test, Playwright, and generated-client boundaries.  Record the local backend
and frontend ports from the prepared repositories.  The two applications may not use the same
defaults in every environment.

## VS Code and IntelliJ IDEA setup

Open both repositories in VS Code or IntelliJ IDEA.  Check that GitHub Copilot Chat is available in
the IDE you plan to use, then record which terminal, task runner, and project view you used for
each command.  The commands and files remain the same, although each IDE exposes them differently.
Keeping that difference visible can help separate an IDE problem from a repository problem.

## Hands-on exercise

Clone `commercial-truck-search-api` and `commercial-truck-search-ui`.  Build, test, and run both
starter repositories without making a feature change.  You can leave OpenSpec uninitialized in
this chapter; the next chapter uses the clean baseline to show what initialization adds.

## Verification checkpoint

Record the baseline commands that succeed, along with the tool versions, known application ports,
and commit IDs.  Before moving on, check that both repositories have passing existing tests and a
clean working tree.  Those commits can serve as reset points for the later exercises.

## What you learned

A known baseline gives later failures a reference point.  If a starter repository does not build or
its existing tests do not pass, fix or record that environment problem before an agent implements
a feature.  That leaves the next chapter free to focus on configuring OpenSpec rather than
debugging an unexamined starting state.
